Brand

A brand kit outlives a project, like the style book: one client buys many spots, and a kit that dies with the job is one you re-upload every time they come back. Each field says what it reaches — a prompt, a compliance check, the Premiere handoff, or a person — because a field that looks like it conditions the frame and does not is worse than one that is absent.

Deliverables

One row per file that leaves the job. A film has one shape; a commercial has fourteen to twenty-two. This set is decided before anything is generated, because it is what says which shots must be shot vertical rather than cropped later — a 9:16 crop of a 16:9 frame keeps 32% of its width, and Auto Reframe cannot invent the two-thirds that were never generated.

Rights

What has been cleared, by whom, where and until when. Recorded, never enforced: nothing here blocks a generation or an export. It is what a delivery has to be able to answer, and the moment to write it down is while you know the answer rather than at delivery.

Titles & Credits

What the film says over its own head and at its end. Both have had routes since the delivery work and neither had a page, so every field could only be written by curl or by an agent. Nothing here generates anything — it is written, ordered, and carried into the export.

Title cards

Credits

Subtitles

One row per cue, in time order. A cue carries its language, who is speaking, where on screen it sits and how it is styled — all of which the route has always accepted and none of which could be typed. Times are in seconds here and stored in milliseconds.

Marketing

Artwork that ships beside the film. Upload something you made in a design tool, or generate it — generation uses the film’s own style preset, so the art looks like the film rather than like a different one.

Consistency Studio

Explore freely when creating. Lock one canonical reference per character/location so storyboards & videos stay consistent. Locked references are injected into production generation.

Budget

s

Published provider rates, with the source and the date each was checked. A rate you override applies to calls made from now on — past events keep the rate they were priced at, so a correction never rewrites history.

Sequences several shots, one move

Select the shots a move travels through, in order, and describe the whole thing. Each pair of neighbouring shots becomes one clip that starts on the first frame and ends on the second — so the movement is between pictures you have already approved, not a guess from a single still. You can also drop in a clip you generated somewhere else.

Blocking

Empty stage.

A NAMED object is blocking: where it stands reaches the image prompt, said from this camera — “in the near foreground at frame left, with its back to camera”. An unnamed one is scaffolding: staged, drawn, and deliberately silent, because describing a nameless box would put a literal box in the frame.

Camera note

One sentence about where the camera is. It LEADS the prompt and is never trimmed, which is why it is capped — put the rest in the description.

Style Book

Shots you like, kept across every film. Give one a name, the camera details you know, and reference visuals. Applying an entry to a shot fills in its scene card — which is what the image and video prompts are built from, so a favourite angle reaches the next generation with nothing else to change.

Settings

Backend Connection

Local endpoints

Off by default. Gridlight needs no API key, so while it was always on it read as “ready” whether or not anything was listening on the port — and it is the fallback every capability drops to. Until you switch it on, nothing resolves to it, and a capability it is the only provider for says nothing serves this rather than failing at generation time.

You

The written-by credit on every screenplay title page and every Final Draft export. Set once here rather than retyped per project — it fills a blank author and never overwrites one, so a screenplay written by someone else keeps their name.

Project Settings

The length this spot is bought at. A conform that misses it by more than a frame refuses rather than trimming — a :30 that arrives at 31.4s is rejected by the station, and one at 29.6s has paid for airtime it did not use. Leave it at 0 for a film, which runs as long as it runs.

Kits live in Brand and outlive this project.

Appended to every image prompt in this project, including the reference plates. Describe a look — lenses, grade, light, texture. Naming a subject here draws it in every frame, whatever the shot is about. The mood board composes this for you; editing it here overwrites what it wrote.

Gallery

Exploring is generated as concepts — kept side by side, and reaching no prompt until you make one the reference. The approved plate is untouched.

New Character

Nothing else tells the model how big this character is, and it is what everything else in frame is measured against.

These four are notes for you and are not sent to an image model — Appearance Prompt is the field that conditions every frame this character appears in.

New Location

Notes for you and for whoever writes the ambient cue. Not sent to a generator — an ambient bed is generated from the scene, not from this field.

New shot

Free text — whatever you would actually search for.

Camera — all optional

Height is what makes a shot read as low or high angle — 0.4m is tatami level, 1.6m is eye level. Leave anything blank you do not know.

Visuals

New Prop

An image model has no sense of scale, and a reference plate makes it worse — a plate is a close-up filling its own frame, so conditioning on one without a size reproduces what it was shown. This is how a 30cm sprinkler comes out the size of a car.

Register Asset

New Music Cue

Comma separated. These reach the generator.

Sent as a style to match, not a track to copy — the clearest music note there is, and it was stored and read by nothing until now.

This is the free text that reaches the prompt. Say what the music DOES against the scene, not only what it sounds like.

Sent to the generator as a negative. A note a composer gives constantly.

Blank scores the measured length of this scene's footage. Set it only to run deliberately past or under the cut.

Leave empty and the cue is one prompt for its whole length. With sections the cue is the sum of its parts and the length above is ignored. Each part runs 3–120 seconds — the generator's own limits.
